newsitem.title: BELGIUM: MEPs agree to new line-ups for January.
newsitem.headline: MEPs agree to new line-ups for January.

text.p: The European Parliament's political groups will see a number of changes on January 1 as part of a mid-term reshuffle.
Italian Claudio Azzolini will become co-president of the 56-member Union for Europe (UPE), parliament's third-largest political group, alongside current French co-president Jean- Claude Pasty.
Magda Alvoet, a Belgian, will become co-president of the 27- member Green group, alongside current German co-president Claudia Roth.
A number of Euro-MPs are also due to change their political family.
Former French development minister Bernard Kouchner is to leave the 215-member Socialist group, parliament's largest political formation, for the 20-member European Radical Alliance.
This follows his decision to join the French Radical Socialist Party in January 1996.
James Janssen van Raay, who left the 182-member Christian Democrat European People's Party (EPP) earlier this month, is to join the UPE.
EPP and UPE officials said the decision appears to have been provoked by a row between the Dutchman and the Dutch Christian Democrat party (CDA).

CDA leader Hans Helchers is believed to have written to Janssen van Raay in early December asking him to honour a promise made three years ago to leave the parliament in 1996, to make way for a younger candidate.
Janssen van Raay, who is serving his third term, chose instead to change parties.
The Dutchman was unavailable for comment on Wednesday.
Moving in the other direction, Italy's Alessandro Fontanta is to leave the UPE for the EPP. A UPE official said Fontanta's political viewpoint was closer to that of the Christian Democrat EPP.
The now dissolved Europe of Nations, led by British anti- federalist billionaire Sir James Goldsmith, was due to announce its reformation last week but has remained mute.
The Socialists announced in early December that their current leader, Pauline Green, would remain in her post for the second half of the legislature, which ends in 1999.
Euro-MPs must elect 14 new vice-presidents and 23 new committee chairpersons in January, when Spanish conservative Jose Maria Gil-Robles takes over from German Klaus Haensch as parliament president.
A month later, on February 1, Julian Priestly will take over from Enrico Vinci as parliament secretary-general.
Priestly is currently a member of Haensch's cabinet.
